samples.summary: Slides has no reachable way to remove a hyperlink once Clear formatting stops doing it
samples.evidence: `slides-view.tsx:738-741` states the link popover is "intentionally unwired — ... Cmd+K no-ops at the editor level until then", and a grep of packages/frontend/src/app/slides/** finds no removeLink/getLinkAtCursor/unlink UI (only the docs popover at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:154 calls removeLink). Slides text-box runs can still gain an href — the shared TextEditor.tryAutoLinkBeforeCursor (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2913) autolinks a typed URL, and PPTX import carries hyperlinks. The new contract says removeLink is the separate command that drops one, but packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:650 removeLink is only exposed on the API, never bound to a toolbar or popover, so after this change a Slides user cannot unlink a run at all (Clear formatting used to). Fix belongs in the Slides UI rather than in the diff.

samples.summary: Cmd+\ now wipes the trailing-edge `href: undefined` pending style, so typing after a clear at a link's end extends the hyperlink
samples.evidence: exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5918-5922) arms pending with { ...visual, href: undefined } so the next typed character escapes the link. clearFormatting() (:3431) *replaces* that pending state with CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, which no longer contains an href key at all; createPendingStyle.set (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:22) overwrites rather than merges, and an absent key in the merge patch means "leave the run's value alone", so text typed after Cmd+\ at a link's trailing edge now inherits the neighbouring run's href. Previously the shortcut's own list carried href: undefined and preserved the escape. The docs toolbar path has the same shape at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1170, where the caret style (including the live href) is merged under the clear patch.

samples.summary: Cmd+\ inside Slides text boxes now also strips fontSize/fontFamily/color/backgroundColor
samples.evidence: initializeTextBox drives the same TextEditor keydown handler (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1238-1242 → clearFormatting), so widening the shortcut's key set to CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE changes behaviour for Slides text boxes and Slides table cells, not just docs — a run's explicit theme-derived font size/family/colour is now removed by the keystroke where it previously survived. Consistent with the toolbar button, but it is a behaviour change in a consumer package the diff does not touch (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:623).

samples.summary: Frontend test comment still describes the old hand-rolled clearFormatting key list
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:967 and :992 ("Same key set as editor.ts clearFormatting() minus `italic`") document a key list that included href and omitted the font/colour keys; the test still passes but now describes a contract that no longer exists.

finding.summary: Slides has no reachable way to remove a hyperlink once Clear formatting stops doing it
finding.evidence: `slides-view.tsx:738-741` states the link popover is "intentionally unwired — ... Cmd+K no-ops at the editor level until then", and a grep of packages/frontend/src/app/slides/** finds no removeLink/getLinkAtCursor/unlink UI (only the docs popover at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:154 calls removeLink). Slides text-box runs can still gain an href — the shared TextEditor.tryAutoLinkBeforeCursor (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2913) autolinks a typed URL, and PPTX import carries hyperlinks. The new contract says removeLink is the separate command that drops one, but packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:650 removeLink is only exposed on the API, never bound to a toolbar or popover, so after this change a Slides user cannot unlink a run at all (Clear formatting used to). Fix belongs in the Slides UI rather than in the diff.

verdict.reason: Repo-wide greps confirm the absence. `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:300-315) no longer clears `href`, and the only non-test invoker of `removeLink` anywhere in the repo is the Docs popover (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-link-popover.tsx:154); the Slides binding at packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:650 is exposed on the API but never called from any UI. The only other href-dropping code (`href: undefined`) is the two removeLink implementations (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3709, packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1244) plus a pending-style escape (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5922) that does not unlink existing runs. Slides is a real consumer of the changed behaviour: text-edit-section.tsx:83 and mobile-toolbar.tsx:576 render the shared TextFormatGroup, whose Clear-formatting button (text-format-group.tsx:151-155,282-296) routes into slides text-box-editor.ts:623 -> CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, and its contract doc (components/text-formatting/types.ts:108-114) still claims href is stripped. Links do reach Slides runs via PPTX import (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:558) and shared autolink (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2902), while slides-view.tsx:738-741 confirms the link popover/Cmd+K is unwired. So a Slides user loses the only unlink affordance with no replacement — a behaviour change to an exported symbol whose other-package consumer silently skips work it used to do.

finding.summary: Cmd+\ now wipes the trailing-edge `href: undefined` pending style, so typing after a clear at a link's end extends the hyperlink
finding.evidence: exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5918-5922) arms pending with { ...visual, href: undefined } so the next typed character escapes the link. clearFormatting() (:3431) *replaces* that pending state with CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, which no longer contains an href key at all; createPendingStyle.set (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:22) overwrites rather than merges, and an absent key in the merge patch means "leave the run's value alone", so text typed after Cmd+\ at a link's trailing edge now inherits the neighbouring run's href. Previously the shortcut's own list carried href: undefined and preserved the escape. The docs toolbar path has the same shape at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1170, where the caret style (including the live href) is merged under the clear patch.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. clearFormatting()'s collapsed-caret path replaces the pending style with CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE (text-editor.ts:3431, reachable from the Cmd+\ handler at text-editor.ts:1238-1242), and CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE contains no `href` key (model/types.ts:300-315, with the doc comment at :283-298 confirming the omission is deliberate). createPendingStyle.set overwrites rather than merges (pending-style.ts:22-24) and consumeForInsert applies the stored patch via applyInlineStyle (:34-40), so an absent `href` leaves the run's href in place. The trailing-edge escape lives only in that pending state: exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge (text-editor.ts:5918-5923) is called only for space (:981), Enter (:2608, :2641) and plain paste (:4154), never for ordinary typed characters, so nothing re-arms it after Cmd+\. The inherited link is real, not hypothetical: applySplitBlock seeds the new block's empty inline with the split-point style, i.e. the link run's style (store/block-helpers.ts:274-277), and the existing test "pressing Enter right after an inserted link starts a plain new paragraph" (test/view/link-trailing-edge.test.ts:163-173) only passes because pending carries href: undefined. Hence Enter-at-trailing-edge → Cmd+\ → typing now yields hyperlinked text. The toolbar path is the same shape and seeds the patch from the raw caret style (which includes the live href at a trailing edge) without merging pending (editor.ts:1167-1174, entered from clearInlineFormatting at :3344-3350). No guard, caller, or test makes this unreachable; it is an invariant relied on by code outside the diff (pending-escape state), so it is in the blast-radius lane and major (silently wrong result on a reachable path).
